title: Ordered 40-byte record assignment
summary: Recovered VA 0x434320: thiscall assignment copies ten DWORDs in ascending order, returns the destination in EAX, and pops the source argument. No calls, global accesses, allocation, floating-point operations, or conditional paths. Direct caller 0x432d69 uses 40-byte indexing and reads the first nine copied words as float triples.
test_description: 800 direct original-versus-C++ comparisons covering distinct, adjacent, identical and every DWORD-aligned overlapping range in both directions. Twenty patterns include zero, all ones, signed zero, infinities, NaNs, subnormal and mixed integer bits. Assert destination return pointer and every word of a 256-byte enclosing buffer against both the oracle and an independent forward-copy model, including untouched source and guard words. Install initialized test-owned FS backing, require successful setup, and check FS:[0] after every original call.
known_limits: Record semantic names and final DWORD type remain unresolved; words are preserved as opaque uint32_t bits.
Tests cover writable DWORD-aligned storage. Invalid pointers, inaccessible memory and byte-misaligned overlap are not exercised; original has no validation.

Partially overlapping record views model original machine storage behavior; portable C++ callers should use live, properly aligned Record40 objects. Such partial object overlap is outside the ordinary C++ object-lifetime model.
No byte-matching claim; native Windows compilation is validated separately by the coordinator.
